subject: SLO gating + peak token runway — post-demo qualification
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya@shipfast.com>; Samir Gupta <samir@shipfast.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: SLO gating + peak token runway — post-demo qualification

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate you walking us through the two demo flows (returns inquiry and conversational routing). Quick recap and the asks we need to move sizing/procurement forward: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct any mistakes):
- Primary latency target: 95th percentile end-to-end ≤ 500ms for interactive routing decisions (sub-500ms is preferred).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~70 QPS during business hours (~1–2 tokens/sec per session on average).
- Peak bursts: short spikes to ~1,000 QPS during promotional windows (peak windows ~5–10 mins).
- Typical payloads: avg 40 tokens/request, tail at ~400 tokens for long assist sessions.
- Streaming: streaming responses used on the routing flow for faster first byte; typical stream duration 1.5–3s.
- Concurrency: ~800 concurrent active sessions during peak; baseline concurrent ~60–80.

What we need from you (deliverables):
1) A one-hour sample trace (JSONL or pcap) with timestamps and token counts for a recent peak and a baseline hour. This helps us produce a working sizing proposal.
2) Confirmation of the absolute latency SLO you want enforced (95th vs 99th; e.g., 95th ≤ 500ms).
3) Any hard constraints for fallbacks (eg. must never route to public model; require private-only inference).

Preliminary Redwood asks / assumptions for sizing (we'll validate with your trace):
- Conservatively assume 3x capacity headroom for autoscale (steady-state cushion + burst absorb).
- For streaming flows, KV-cache reuse is low; plan per-token CPU/GPU time accordingly.
- Pilot: 48-hour pilot with synthetic burst replay is helpful to validate backpressure and tail latency.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Priya: send sample traces + confirm SLOs by EOD Wed (10/21).
- Redwood: produce an initial sizing + rough cost range within 48 hours of receiving traces.
- If sizing looks good: schedule a 30–60m engineering sync to lock down network/procurement asklist and pilot start date.

Attachments: please upload the trace to the Drive link or attach directly — small sample files are fine.

Thanks — looping Marissa for procurement coordination and Laura for any streaming-specific config notes.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLO gating + peak token runway — post-demo qualification

Thanks Jordan — good summary. Quick answers and I attached the baseline + a recent peak hour sample. See inline: 

- SLO: we'll target 95th ≤ 500ms for routing decisions; for the long assist session path 95th ≤ 900ms is acceptable (customers tolerate longer on heavy generation).
- Steady-state: our telemetry shows ~65–75 QPS during business hours (US east coast timezone).
- Peak: marketing campaigns historically cause 7–12 min bursts; we've seen instantaneous spikes to ~1k QPS.
- Tokens: median 38 tokens; 90th 210; 99th ~420. Streaming first-byte is important for UX (we measure conversion lift).
- Concurrency: baseline concurrent sessions ~70; observed peaks ~850.
- Fallbacks: prefer private-only inference for PII workloads; public model fallback allowed for anonymized routing only.

Attachments included: traffic_sample-202609.jsonl (contains two 1-hour windows: baseline and a peak). Also sharing a short procurement note on timelines — procurement-checklist-SF.docx.

Procurement timeline: legal review + SOC2 evidence expected to be 2–3 weeks; if we pilot earlier we can use an interim NDPA. Samir is looped for signoff on timing.

Let us know if you need different formatting for the trace.

— Priya

Subject: Re: SLO gating + peak token runway — post-demo qualification

Got the samples — thanks Priya, this is very helpful. A few notes from a quick pass through the peak window followed by an ask-list so we can size accurately: 

Quick observations (preliminary):
- Median tokens (38) and 99th (~420) match what you reported.
- Burst shape: ~60% of the 10-min burst is concentrated in two 90s crests; that pattern drives slotting/instance warm strategy.
- Streaming: first-byte latency is the main UX metric; our runtime can hit ~200–350ms first-byte on dedicated CUDA instances for 40-token requests, but long tail depends on concurrency and serialization.

Redwood initial sizing proposal (attached PDF shows math):
- Baseline pool: target to support 75 QPS steady-state with 2x headroom = N small GPU workers (see attachment).
- Burst runway: to handle 1k QPS spikes we recommend a transient burst pool with pre-warmed replicas sized to absorb the crest (3–5 minute pre-warm).
- Concurrency tuning: target per-worker concurrent sessions ~12 for streaming to keep 95th latency under 500ms; we recommend session-aware bin-packing.

Pilot ask & next steps:
1) Authorization to run a 48-hour pilot in your test VPC (or Redwood-hosted isolated slice) replaying the peak sample — this will validate tail and autoscale timings.
2) Permission to ingest anonymized telemetry (token counts, timestamps, success/fail). We'll produce a data-handling plan and minimal retention.
3) If pilot looks good, Marissa will scope procurement and provide a formal pricing band.

I've attached a short-sizing PDF with expected instance counts, estimated token/sec capacity, and a rough cost band for the pilot. If you approve the pilot run, Laura and I can schedule a 30m engineering kickoff tomorrow.

— Jordan
